problem: Text-goal instance navigation needs the agent to pick the right instance among same-category distractors. Prior methods reduce long descriptions to category labels or short attributes and use them only for verification. They ignore the spatial context in the caption, and their matching is viewpoint-biased. Interactive agents also need a human in the loop.
motivation: Surrounding context in a long description is a strong constraint that narrows the search space and separates distractors. Relations such as 'left of' depend on the narrator's unknown viewpoint, so viewpoint-agnostic checks give plausible but wrong stops. The paper therefore uses the full caption as an exploration signal and verifies spatial relations explicitly in 3D.
key_idea: Use the full contextual caption as a dense text-image value map for frontier selection, then accept a candidate only if its caption relations hold from at least one sampled observer viewpoint in the online 3D instance map.
insight: Encoding the full caption with a token-level-grounded CLIP (GOAL) gives the best exploration prior. GOAL-CLIP with full text reaches 20.3 SR, versus 13.7 with category only and 16.7 with intrinsic attributes. BLIP-2 gains little in SR from full text, so token-level grounding matters. In the component ablation, replacing value-map frontiers with nearest-frontier costs 9.7 SR, and removing context verification costs 8.3 SR. Every module is therefore load-bearing.
method: Perception: GroundingDINO detection with FastSAM masks. COCO classes are confirmed by YOLOv7; open-set classes are confirmed by a VLM yes/no query. Verified instances are fused into a landmark cloud.
Instance-level 3D mapping: observations are merged by a 2D-center proximity heuristic, with a fallback to voxel-overlap similarity normalized by the smaller set.

Wall-only map: height-gated (0.8-3 m) depth points are segmented into vertical planes with RANSAC and rasterized. Connected components of free space define rooms, and line-of-sight is ray-cast through the wall layer.
Context-driven value map: GOAL-CLIP encodes the full caption and each RGB frame. Per-pixel similarities are projected to a top-down value map (VLFM-style), and the highest-value frontier is chosen.

Room-level override: once a target is detected and a context object is still unseen in its room, the nearest unexplored frontier in that room is chosen exactly once. Low-level motion uses a depth-only VER PointNav policy.

Intrinsic verification: an LLM turns the caption into paraphrased yes/unknown/no prompts, and a VLM scores 0-15 with the instance highlighted. Unknown answers are re-queried on the best of the next five frames, ranked by text-image similarity.

Extrinsic verification: after a same-room check (3 m), 24 bearings times 4 radii (0.8-2.0 m) of viewpoints are sampled around each anchor. Each viewpoint gets a local frame aligned to the reference object. Seven predicates (left, right, front, behind, near, above, below) must all hold at one viewpoint.

setting.backbone: GOAL-CLIP (frozen) for the value map; GroundingDINO, FastSAM and YOLOv7 for detection; an LLM for caption parsing and a VLM for attribute VQA (both frozen); a pretrained VER PointNav policy for low-level motion
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward, turn-left, turn-right, stop, with waypoints executed by a PointNav policy

numbers.extra: success radius 1 m, max 1000 steps; 1000 episodes

numbers.evidence: Table 1, CoIN-Bench Val Seen Synonyms, Ours

numbers_note: InstanceNav is not a canonical benchmark name and CoIN-Bench is reported with three splits (val-seen, val-seen-synonyms, val-unseen), so both use 'other:' names. The paper gives no explicit split name for InstanceNav, so 'test' is inferred from 'the test set contains 1,000 episodes'.
results: Context-Nav gets the best SR on InstanceNav (26.2, versus the re-run PSL at 26.0 and UniGoal at 20.2) and on all three CoIN-Bench splits. On CoIN-Bench it gets 13.5, 20.3 and 11.3 SR, against AIUTA's 7.4, 14.4 and 6.7 and PSL's 8.8, 8.9 and 4.6. On InstanceNav its SPL (9.1) is below UniGoal's 11.4.
limitations: Compute-heavy pipeline with many stacked models (detector, segmenter, VLM, LLM, CLIP). The authors list reducing computational latency as future work.

Absolute success rates remain low (about 11-26% SR). Relation semantics are handcrafted geometric predicates that need tightening, and the first-stage evidence is only ablated on one CoIN-Bench split.
Only simulated HM3D benchmarks are evaluated, with no real-robot tests. InstanceNav SPL is lower than UniGoal's.
